# Cortex Website — Master Specification

## 1. Purpose
This document consolidates the website-related decisions, requirements, architecture, legal requirements, conversion flow, design rules, multi-tenant requirements, implementation phases, and launch controls discussed in this conversation.

## 2. Company Positioning
- Cortex is a data-first enterprise operational intelligence company/platform.
<!-- SPEC-000001: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex operates multi-agent solutions for enterprise problems.
<!-- SPEC-000002: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Enterprise data is the foundation.
<!-- SPEC-000003: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex reconstructs operational state from fragmented enterprise data.
<!-- SPEC-000004: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex models relationships, dependencies, and constraints.
<!-- SPEC-000005: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex evaluates possible consequences.
<!-- SPEC-000006: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex coordinates specialized intelligence.
<!-- SPEC-000007: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex applies policy and safety boundaries.
<!-- SPEC-000008: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex supports controlled enterprise execution.
<!-- SPEC-000009: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cortex records outcomes and decision memory.
<!-- SPEC-000010: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Supply-chain disruption and mitigation is the first commercial wedge.
<!-- SPEC-000011: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Supply chain is not the permanent category of the company.
<!-- SPEC-000012: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The broader category is enterprise operational intelligence.
<!-- SPEC-000013: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as a generic chatbot.
<!-- SPEC-000014: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as a generic AI copilot.
<!-- SPEC-000015: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as an ERP replacement.
<!-- SPEC-000016: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as a dashboard.
<!-- SPEC-000017: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as an LLM wrapper.
<!-- SPEC-000018: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website must not position Cortex primarily as a forecasting-only system.
<!-- SPEC-000019: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- A core positioning direction is: The intelligence layer for complex operations.
<!-- SPEC-000020: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- A concise system framing is: Understand. Simulate. Decide. Act.
<!-- SPEC-000021: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The site should make clear that AI is not the foundation; data and operational state are.
<!-- SPEC-000022: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 4. Corrected Design System
- Background: #FAFAFA.
<!-- SPEC-000049: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Primary text: #111111.
<!-- SPEC-000050: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Sole accent: #16A34A.
<!-- SPEC-000051: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Failure/error state: #DC2626.
<!-- SPEC-000052: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Green is used for the primary CTA.
<!-- SPEC-000053: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Green is used for links.
<!-- SPEC-000054: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Green is used for verified/pass states.
<!-- SPEC-000055: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Green is not decorative.
<!-- SPEC-000056: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Red is used only for actual failure/error output states.
<!-- SPEC-000057: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Red is not decorative.
<!-- SPEC-000058: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Typeface: Inter.
<!-- SPEC-000059: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Inter is used for headings.
<!-- SPEC-000060: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Inter is used for body copy.
<!-- SPEC-000061: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Inter is used for UI.
<!-- SPEC-000062: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Inter is used for navigation.
<!-- SPEC-000063: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Inter is used for buttons.
<!-- SPEC-000064: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- JetBrains Mono is used only for actual code.
<!-- SPEC-000065: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- JetBrains Mono is used only for commands.
<!-- SPEC-000066: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- JetBrains Mono is used only for terminal output.
<!-- SPEC-000067: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- JetBrains Mono is used only for receipt/JSON output when fixed-width formatting is functional.
<!-- SPEC-000068: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- JetBrains Mono is not decorative.
<!-- SPEC-000069: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Fixed type scale: 14px, 16px, 20px, 28px, 40px.
<!-- SPEC-000070: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Body line-height: 1.5.
<!-- SPEC-000071: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Heading line-height: 1.2.
<!-- SPEC-000072: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Avoid arbitrary font sizes per section.
<!-- SPEC-000073: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Use systematic spacing.
<!-- SPEC-000074: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Use whitespace to establish hierarchy.
<!-- SPEC-000075: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Borders should establish structure rather than decoration.
<!-- SPEC-000076: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 5. Copy Rules
- Write in plain English.
<!-- SPEC-000077: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “revolutionize.”
<!-- SPEC-000078: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “empower.”
<!-- SPEC-000079: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “seamless.”
<!-- SPEC-000080: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “next-generation.”
<!-- SPEC-000081: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “cutting-edge.”
<!-- SPEC-000082: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Ban “game-changing.”
<!-- SPEC-000083: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Avoid generic competitor-swappable claims.
<!-- SPEC-000084: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Prefer statements describing actual system behavior.
<!-- SPEC-000085: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Prefer observable claims over adjectives.
<!-- SPEC-000086: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Prefer exact operational descriptions.
<!-- SPEC-000087: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Every claim should be checkable against actual product behavior, actual receipt/output, documented methodology, or explicitly labelled demonstration.
<!-- SPEC-000088: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- If a claim cannot be verified, remove it or label it as future capability.
<!-- SPEC-000089: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not use inflated adjectives as a substitute for evidence.
<!-- SPEC-000090: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Preferred claim pattern: “Runs your test suite in an isolated container with no network access, then signs the result.”
<!-- SPEC-000091: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent customers.
<!-- SPEC-000092: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent testimonials.
<!-- SPEC-000093: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent metrics.
<!-- SPEC-000094: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent certifications.
<!-- SPEC-000095: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent pricing.
<!-- SPEC-000096: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not invent production capabilities.
<!-- SPEC-000097: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 6. Marketing Website vs Product
- The public website and authenticated Cortex application are separate surfaces.
<!-- SPEC-000098: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site explains the company.
<!-- SPEC-000099: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site explains the platform.
<!-- SPEC-000100: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site establishes trust.
<!-- SPEC-000101: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site converts visitors into qualified conversations.
<!-- SPEC-000102: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site may use curated product screenshots.
<!-- SPEC-000103: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site may use real terminal recordings.
<!-- SPEC-000104: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site may use real receipt JSON snippets.
<!-- SPEC-000105: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site may use controlled demonstrations.
<!-- SPEC-000106: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Synthetic demonstrations must be explicitly labelled.
<!-- SPEC-000107: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Live enterprise results must be explicitly labelled.
<!-- SPEC-000108: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site must never expose customer operational data.
<!-- SPEC-000109: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site must not contain privileged application credentials.
<!-- SPEC-000110: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site must not directly query customer operational databases.
<!-- SPEC-000111: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The public site must not become a clone of the authenticated product.
<!-- SPEC-000112: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The marketing site may reuse visual primitives but must not depend on live customer operational state.
<!-- SPEC-000113: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The actual product is where tenant data, world state, intelligence, agents, execution, and memory operate.
<!-- SPEC-000114: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

### Problem
- Explain that enterprise data tells organizations what happened but does not automatically tell them what to do next.
<!-- SPEC-000174: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Show fragmented sources such as ERP, WMS, TMS, procurement, planning, internal systems, and other enterprise data.
<!-- SPEC-000175: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Explain that decisions cross system boundaries.
<!-- SPEC-000176: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Conceptual pipeline: DATA -> WORLD MODEL -> REASONING -> SIMULATION -> DECISION -> ACTION.
<!-- SPEC-000177: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

### Controlled Autonomy
- READ -> REASON -> SIMULATE -> POLICY -> APPROVAL -> EXECUTE -> OBSERVE.
<!-- SPEC-000212: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

<!-- SPEC-000213: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Specialist agents may PROPOSE where permitted.
<!-- SPEC-000214: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Specialist agents should not directly EXECUTE where the security architecture denies execution.
<!-- SPEC-000215: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Execution belongs to the controlled execution layer.
<!-- SPEC-000216: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- This boundary should be prominent because it is an enterprise trust mechanism.
<!-- SPEC-000217: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 29. Multi-Tenant Architecture
- Build one multi-tenant system.
<!-- SPEC-000465: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not duplicate applications per customer.
<!-- SPEC-000466: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Tenant context must be resolved centrally.
<!-- SPEC-000467: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Tenant context should be derived from authenticated identity or API key/session at the earliest reliable middleware layer.
<!-- SPEC-000468: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not re-derive tenant identity independently in every endpoint.
<!-- SPEC-000469: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Organization model is the tenant foundation.
<!-- SPEC-000470: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Organization -> Project -> ApiKey/Device relationships remain the base where correct.
<!-- SPEC-000471: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Shared database plus tenant/organization foreign keys is the correct starting architecture at pre-launch scale.
<!-- SPEC-000472: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not build schema-per-tenant prematurely.
<!-- SPEC-000473: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not build database-per-tenant prematurely.
<!-- SPEC-000474: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Stronger isolation can be added when a real enterprise contract requires it.
<!-- SPEC-000475: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 31. Authentication and Authorization
- Authentication maps users/API keys to organizations.
<!-- SPEC-000482: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- require_api_key must resolve organization context.
<!-- SPEC-000483: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- API key is a path to tenant context, not the tenant identity itself.
<!-- SPEC-000484: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Authorization must verify principal access to organization and resource.
<!-- SPEC-000485: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Project access is organization-scoped.
<!-- SPEC-000486: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Device access is organization-scoped.
<!-- SPEC-000487: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Resource lookup should not rely on resource ID alone when tenant-scoped.
<!-- SPEC-000488: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 32. Data Isolation
- Tenant-scoped tables should carry organization_id or equivalent.
<!-- SPEC-000489: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Repository queries must scope by tenant.
<!-- SPEC-000490: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Use compound lookups such as organization_id + resource ID.
<!-- SPEC-000491: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Use database constraints where appropriate.
<!-- SPEC-000492: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Add negative isolation tests.
<!-- SPEC-000493: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Organization A must never see Organization B data.
<!-- SPEC-000494: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Organization A credentials must never authorize Organization B resources.
<!-- SPEC-000495: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Resource identifiers alone must not bypass tenant authorization.
<!-- SPEC-000496: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 33. Statelessness
- Production services should be stateless.
<!-- SPEC-000497: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not depend on process-local dictionaries for durable state.
<!-- SPEC-000498: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The earlier in-memory _runs approach is demo-only and must not become production architecture.
<!-- SPEC-000499: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Shared persistence is required for horizontally scaled services.
<!-- SPEC-000500: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Session state belongs in shared infrastructure.
<!-- SPEC-000501: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Rate-limit state belongs in shared infrastructure when required.
<!-- SPEC-000502: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Do not assume requests return to the same container.
<!-- SPEC-000503: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 34. Caching
- Do not add a cache until useful.
<!-- SPEC-000504: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- If caching is added, keys must include tenant context.
<!-- SPEC-000505: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Example: organization_id:resource.
<!-- SPEC-000506: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Never globally cache tenant-scoped resources.
<!-- SPEC-000507: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Cache invalidation must preserve tenant scope.
<!-- SPEC-000508: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 35. Rate Limiting
- Rate limiting is per organization.
<!-- SPEC-000509: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Fixed window is acceptable for an initial implementation if adequate.
<!-- SPEC-000510: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Sliding window/token bucket can be introduced later.
<!-- SPEC-000511: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Shared state is required when horizontally scaling.
<!-- SPEC-000512: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Rate-limit behavior should not reveal sensitive tenant data.
<!-- SPEC-000513: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 36. Monitoring
- Track request volume by organization.
<!-- SPEC-000514: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Track errors by organization.

<!-- SPEC-000516: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Track relevant usage metrics by organization.

- Alert on noisy tenants.
<!-- SPEC-000518: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

- Avoid logging source code or secrets.
<!-- SPEC-000520: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

| No decorative AI aesthetic | No gradients/glass/orbs/mesh/particles | Global |
<!-- SPEC-000799: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Demo conversion | Multi-step enterprise intake | /demo |
<!-- SPEC-000800: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Legal | Terms/privacy/AUP/responsible AI/cookies | /legal |
<!-- SPEC-000801: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Security | Tenant isolation and capability boundaries | /security |
<!-- SPEC-000802: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Multi-tenancy | Shared DB + tenant context | Product backend |
<!-- SPEC-000803: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Tenant settings | Organization settings | Accounts/API |
<!-- SPEC-000804: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Rate limiting | Per organization | Accounts/API |
<!-- SPEC-000805: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Product boundary | Marketing has no customer data access | Architecture |
<!-- SPEC-000806: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Evidence | Real outputs | Homepage/Research |
<!-- SPEC-000807: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Synthetic labeling | Controlled Synthetic Demonstration | Proof |
<!-- SPEC-000808: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
| Live labeling | Live Enterprise Pilot Validation | Proof |
<!-- SPEC-000809: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->

## 54. Final Direction
- Cortex should look like a serious enterprise technology company whose product uses advanced AI.
<!-- SPEC-000810: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The website should not look like an AI marketing template.
<!-- SPEC-000811: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest visual language is evidence, structure, typography, restrained motion, and precise state changes.
<!-- SPEC-000812: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest copy language is direct description of what the system actually does.
<!-- SPEC-000813: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest proof is a real receipt, real command, real screenshot, documented evaluation, or approved live result.
<!-- SPEC-000814: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest security story is a boundary between data, intelligence, agents, policy, approval, execution, and memory.
<!-- SPEC-000815: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest commercial story is that Cortex starts with supply-chain disruption but is built for broader complex operations.
<!-- SPEC-000816: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- The strongest SaaS architecture is one multi-tenant system with centralized tenant context, shared infrastructure, tenant-scoped data, configuration, stateless services, tenant-aware caching, and per-organization monitoring/rate limiting.
<!-- SPEC-000817: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- No page should exist merely because enterprise websites normally have that page.
<!-- SPEC-000818: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
- Every page must explain something, prove something, convert someone, establish trust, or satisfy a real legal/security requirement.
<!-- SPEC-000819: verify this requirement during implementation and launch QA. -->
